html:
The Continuation War was fought by Finland against the Soviet Union from 1941 to 1944, alongside Nazi Germany but not formally allied to it.

Finland joined the German attack on the Soviet Union to win back the land lost in the Winter War. Its army retook Karelia and went beyond the old border, taking part in the siege of Leningrad from the north. In summer 1944 a huge Soviet offensive broke through, but the Finns stopped it at Tali-Ihantala.

Finland then made peace, gave up the lost land again and had to drive the German troops out of Lapland. It paid heavy reparations to the Soviet Union, but it was never occupied and kept its democracy, unlike the Baltic states. The result shaped Finland's careful policy towards Moscow. See Finland.
sum: The Continuation War was fought by Finland against the Soviet Union from 1941 to 1944, alongside Nazi Germany but not formally allied to it.
